questions.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the ellipsoid $\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{5}+\frac{(z-3)^{2}}{2}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipsoid:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}+\frac{{0}^{2}}{5}+\frac{(z-3)^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{8}+\frac{(z-3)^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}+\frac{(z-3)^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of the ellipse with semi-axes $2\sqrt{2}$ and $\sqrt{2},$ centered at $(0,3)$ in the $xz$-plane.

questions.problem: What is the trace in the $xy$-plane of the ellipsoid $\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{8}+\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{2}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xy$-plane, we substitute $z=0$ into the equation of the ellipsoid:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{8}+\frac{(0+1)^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{8} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{8}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of the ellipse with semi-axes $2\sqrt{2}$ and $2,$ centered at $(1,3)$ in the $xy$-plane.

questions.problem: What is the projection of the intersection between the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+(z-3)^{2}=13$ and the plane $y=3$ onto the $xz$-plane.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the sphere and the plane $y=3$, we substitute $y=3$ into the equation of the sphere:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+(3)^{2}+(z-3)^{2} & =13 \\ {x}^{2}+9+(z-3)^{2} & =13 \\ {x}^{2}+(z-3)^{2} & =4 \\ {x}^{2}+(z-3)^{2} & ={2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Projecting this onto the $xz$-plane gives us the equation of the circle of radius $2$ centered at $(0,3).$

questions.problem: Given the ellipsoid $\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{11}=1$, find its intercepts with the $z$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $z$-intercepts, we plug $x=0$ and $y=0$ into the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(0+1)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(0-2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{11} & =1 \\ \frac{1}{4}+\frac{4}{9}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{11} & =1 \\ \frac{{z}^{2}}{11} & =\frac{11}{36} \\ {z}^{2} & =\frac{121}{36} \\ z & =\pm \frac{11}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the solutions $z=-\frac{11}{6}$ and $z=\frac{11}{6}.$

Therefore, the intercepts with the $z$-axis are $(0,0,-\frac{11}{6})$ and $(0,0,\frac{11}{6}).$
